Warren is a quiet rural county where homes are inexpensive and almost nothing new gets built. The July 2025 estimate is 5,269 people, compared with 5,834 in the 2010 count and 5,215 in 2020. Warrenton is the seat, and Camak and Norwood are the other towns.

When a house is worth that little, a few years of unpaid tax plus interest can swallow a large piece of the price. Pay attention to old balances early, and ask about them before you set an asking price. Median household income is $44,289, and buyers who work from home will want to check internet service at the specific address.

Georgia's default is December 20, though a county board can pull the date forward to December 1 or November 15 or use installments. The tax commissioner can tell you which schedule your bill follows. Every owner gets 60 days after the postmark before interest starts.

The city of Warrenton, Warren County itself, the school system and the state each levy tax as of January 1, and every parcel is assessed at 40% of market value. For the current millage rate, ask the commissioner about your parcel or read the county finance page, where the commissioners publish a current digest and a five-year history of levy. Tax hearings are advertised whenever a proposed millage rate exceeds the rollback rate.

  • Returns run January 1 to April 1. If you skip one, last year's value rolls forward.
  • A mobile home owner applies for a location permit within 30 days of placing the unit, then renews each year in the same window.
  • Overpayments can be reclaimed if the request starts within three years.

Put the appeal in writing and send it to the assessors' board, carrying a postmark within 45 days of the mailing date printed on your notice. Acceptable reasons are taxability, value, uniformity and denied exemptions. Mail it to the county board rather than the state, which cannot take it.

Form PT-311A makes you choose a path. Most owners choose the equalization board route. A hearing officer only hears non-homestead real estate worth more than $500,000, and arbitration needs a certified appraisal that you supply.

If you are still unhappy, a written notice for superior court has to reach the county board within a month of the hearing officer's, arbitrator's or Board of Equalization's decision, and taxes must be paid at last year's level before a judge hears the case. If the final value ends at 85% or less of the earlier figure, the owner recovers litigation costs and attorney's fees.

Warren adds no local exemption of its own, so owners rely on the statewide ones. The form goes in at any point after the home becomes your primary residence, and it needs to arrive by April 1 for the first year you want relief. Missing that date forfeits the exemption for the year.

The tax commissioner's staff handle these applications. Carry proof that you live in the house and ask which age or disability categories you could add. A buyer who will live in the house files a new form of their own, which is worth mentioning when the closing falls late in the year.

The tax commissioner is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, phone 706-465-2231, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321. Staff take card payments by phone, and an online option is linked from the commissioner's page, so ask about fees when you call.

sections.h2: How a sale closes out the tax bill
sections.html:
The bill follows whoever owned the property on January 1, so sellers and buyers split it on the settlement statement. Ask the commissioner for a written balance that covers each year up to the closing date, then give that paper to the closing attorney. A house inside Warrenton, Camak or Norwood may owe a city levy on top of the county one.

  • Get separate figures for the county, the school district and any city.
  • Check whether a mobile home or timber account sits under the same name.
  • Keep your receipts for three years in case a refund claim comes up.

In a market with few buyers, an owner who arrives with a clear title and paid-up taxes has an easier path to closing. Heirs with an old family house in town or out on a rural road should ask the commissioner for every open year before listing, since a small balance carried for a long time can grow past what the house will bring. A buyer paying cash and taking the house as it stands can settle those years from the proceeds in one step, with no repair list and no wait for a lender's appraisal.

sections.h2: Steps before you list a Warren County house
sections.html:
Begin with the commissioner on Main Street. Ask for the balance on every account under your name, including any mobile home or timber account, and ask which schedule your bill follows. Then call the assessors and confirm that your homestead exemption is on file and that the acreage and building details on the record match the property.

Next, find your deed. If a copy is missing, ask the clerk's office for one before a buyer's attorney asks. A family house that passed down without paperwork can need extra title work, and that slows a closing more than any tax balance does.

Finally, tell the closing attorney who owned the property on January 1 and which bills are still open. The attorney will pull the written payoff from the commissioner, add the city levy if the house is inside a town, and show the split between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. If a buyer will live in the house, remind them to file their own homestead form, since yours does not carry over.

Owners who inherited a house far from Warrenton can do most of this by phone and mail. Ask the commissioner to send the balance in writing, and keep every receipt, because a refund claim for an overpayment has a three-year window. If you cannot reach the office during the week, write down your parcel number and questions in advance so one call covers everything, and ask staff to confirm any figure by email or letter. A written number protects you if the closing date moves and the balance changes with it.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Warren County tax bill?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner does, at 706-465-2231. The office is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321.

faqs.q: By when must a Warren County value dispute be mailed?
faqs.a: Your envelope needs a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing date. Address it to the county's assessors in writing. State offices do not take these appeals.

faqs.q: Is there a Warren County exemption beyond the state homestead one?
faqs.a: No. Owners use the statewide homestead exemptions and apply by April 1 for the first year.

faqs.q: What percentage of value does Warren County tax?
faqs.a: Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value. Exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I give a card number over the phone to pay Warren County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Staff take card payments by phone, and an online option is available too. Call 706-465-2231 to ask about fees.
